topicFamilies.label: Adult OSA PAP — CPAP/APAP/BPAP treatment and support
topicFamilies.authorityBoundary: Adult OSA PAP route only. Do not use this family as current CSA/ASV treatment authority or as a hypoventilation/NIV algorithm.

topicFamilies.label: Adult OSA manual CPAP/BPAP titration
topicFamilies.authorityBoundary: Use for OSA CPAP/BPAP titration workflow. Its pressure-adjustment logic must not be generalized to ASV or NIV.

topicFamilies.label: Adult CSA PAP and ASV treatment context
topicFamilies.authorityBoundary: The 2025 AASM adult CSA guideline leads clinical treatment selection, but actual ASV administration also requires the current label/IFU for the device used. The ResMed AirCurve 11 ASV contraindication is a device-specific safety overlay, not a universal cross-manufacturer ASV rule. Both the clinical-indication gate and the actual-device safety gate must be satisfied.

topicFamilies.label: Treatment-emergent central events during PAP
topicFamilies.authorityBoundary: First recognize and score the respiratory pattern correctly; then use the current CSA treatment pathway. Do not respond to central events by automatically applying the OSA obstructive pressure-increase algorithm.

topicFamilies.label: Hypoventilation and NIV / ventilation-support preparation
topicFamilies.authorityBoundary: The AASM NPPV position paper supplies an active-listed but older ventilation framework and must be currentness-watched. Current AASM scoring and CO2 monitoring guidance control rule-sensitive scoring/monitoring. Mode-specific NIV settings, target volumes, alarms, pressure support, backup-rate details and device operation still require the current order, facility protocol, manufacturer instructions and diagnosis-specific guidance; no universal modern NIV titration algorithm is inferred.

topicFamilies.label: Obesity hypoventilation syndrome — CPAP versus NIV context
topicFamilies.authorityBoundary: ATS 2019 provides current OHS-specific specialty guidance. In stable ambulatory OHS with coexistent severe OSA, CPAP is the first-line PAP branch rather than automatic NIV. This OHS-specific pathway must not be generalized to every hypoventilation syndrome, and treatment changes remain clinician-directed.

topicFamilies.label: Cross-modality PAP comfort, interface, education, and adherence support
topicFamilies.authorityBoundary: Interface, comfort, communication, and adherence support can be taught across PAP contexts, but this family does not decide the diagnosis, treatment indication, modality, or device settings.

topicFamilies.label: PAP device, order, facility, and manufacturer boundary
topicFamilies.authorityBoundary: Device menus, mode names, contraindications, setup sequences, limits, alarms, backup-rate settings, target-volume behavior and escalation thresholds are not universal. Verify the actual device label/IFU, order, facility SOP and applicable scope requirements. A single manufacturer's ASV labeling must not be generalized to other devices.
